# Appeal of Denial — Rotator Cuff Repair (CPT 29827)

**Member:** Reese Iverson
**Member ID:** W233165693
**Plan:** Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Louisiana (Commercial/ACA)
**Reference Number:** POC-757C3B7E16-21498
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-06
**Governing Policy:** Carelon Joint Surgery 2025-11-15 (HTML) — https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/

Dear Appeals Review Team,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), as stated in the notice dated 2026-08-06, reference number POC-757C3B7E16-21498. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider its decision.

## The Denial's Stated Reason

The notice states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I want to address this directly, using the record of my own care.

## What My Records Show

According to the clinical summary in my prior authorization packet:

- I have had progressive shoulder pain for **18 months**, unrelieved by rest.
- I completed **16 weeks of supervised physical therapy** (16 visits, from 2026-02-24 to 2026-06-16), focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- I used **NSAIDs for 8 months** with inadequate relief.
- I received a **corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-30**, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- An **MRI on 2026-07-07** confirmed a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy.
- On exam, I have limited range of motion due to pain and positive provocative testing, and I am unable to lift my arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side.

This is a documented, multi-month course of conservative treatment — physical therapy, medication, and an injection — that did not resolve my symptoms, alongside imaging confirming a structural tear that my surgeon has identified as the cause.

## A Note on the Policy Criteria Provided to Me

I want to be transparent about what I am and am not able to quote in this letter. The policy excerpts I currently have in hand from the Carelon Joint Surgery guideline address medical necessity criteria for shoulder **arthroplasty, hemiarthroplasty, and reverse shoulder arthroplasty** — not the specific criteria the plan applies to **rotator cuff repair**. Because those excerpts do not address my procedure, I am not quoting them here as if they justify my case; that would not accurately reflect what the plan has published for this specific service.

This is precisely why I am formally requesting, in writing, that the plan identify and provide the specific medical necessity criteria it applied when denying CPT 29827 for insufficient conservative care. The plan holds these criteria and is in the best position to state exactly what standard my records were measured against. My plan uses Carelon for musculoskeletal surgery, and Carelon publishes its guidelines without a login; I am asking that the plan point me and my surgeon to the exact rotator cuff repair section of the current Joint Surgery guideline it used to reach this denial, so that we can confirm whether my documented care meets it.

## What I Am Asking

I am asking the plan to:

1. Reconsider the denial in light of the 18-month symptom duration, 16-week completed physical therapy course, 8 months of NSAID use, corticosteroid injection, and MRI-confirmed full-thickness tear documented in my records; and
2. Provide, in writing, the specific rotator cuff repair conservative-care criteria applied to my request, so that my surgeon and I can respond to the precise standard at issue.

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-02** (180 days from the date of the denial notice). Please send it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, or I will confirm the correct address by calling the number on the back of my insurance card and asking where member appeals are filed.

Thank you for reconsidering my case. Please let me know if any additional records are needed.

Sincerely,

[Reese Iverson]
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

quotes: shoulder arthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications:

Limited range of motion or crepitus of the glenohumeral joint on physical examination Pain and loss of function of at least 6 months’ duration that interferes with daily activities (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4) *Radiographic evidence of destructive degenerative joint disease as evidenced by marked joint space narrowing AND ONE or more of the following:

Irregular joint surfaces Glenoid sclerosis Osteophyte changes Flattened glenoid Cystic changes in the humeral head Failure of conservative management of at least 6 weeks’ duration (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 or diffuse modified Outerbridge grade III-IV changes) Hemiarthroplasty Hemiarthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications:

Proximal humerus fracture confirmed by imaging not amenable to internal fixation (e.g., severe comminution, poor bone quality, multi-part, displaced) Malignancy involving the glenohumeral joint or surrounding soft tissue Advanced joint disease of the shoulder when criteria for total shoulder arthroplasty are met AND at least ONE of the following conditions is present:

Osteonecrosis of the humeral head without glenoid involvement Glenoid bone stock inadequate to support a glenoid prosthesis Advanced joint disease due to rotator cuff tear arthropathy* Glenohumeral osteoarthritis with irreparable rotator cuff tear* *except for Exclusions listed below Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty Reverse shoulder arthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications:

Deficient rotator cuff with limited ability to actively flex the upper extremity above the plane of the shoulder Revision or Replacement of a Shoulder Prosthesis Revision or replacement of a shoulder prosthesis is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following conditions when associated with pain and functional impairment:
Preoperative investigation using serologic testing and IF there are abnormal laboratory findings, at least ONE of the following:

Synovial fluid testing, such as leukocyte count and neutrophil percentage, aerobic and anaerobic bacterial cultures, leukocyte esterase, alpha defensin testing (Synovasure®), synovial fluid CRP, synovial fluid PCR for bacteria Intraoperative plan for histopathology and/or aerobic and anaerobic tissue cultures using implant sonication for cultures or PCR Contraindications All procedures listed in this guideline are contraindicated when ANY of the following conditions are present:

Active infection of the joint Active systemic bacteremia Active skin infection or open wound at the surgical site Rapidly progressive neurologic disease Intra-articular corticosteroid injection within the past 6 weeks in the joint being replaced Exclusions Indications other than those addressed in this guideline are considered not medically necessary including, but not limited to, the following:

Shoulder arthroplasty under conditions which would result in excessive stress on the implant including, but not limited to, Charcot joint and paralytic conditions of the shoulder Shoulder resurfacing, including total, hemi, or partial resurfacing (e.g., Copeland™, the Extended Articulating Surface (EAS)™ Resurfacing Heads, Global CAP™ CTA Resurfacing Shoulder Humeral Head)
